item.title: American Bitcoin (ABTC) Posts $126 Million Profit as Holdings Gain $197 Million
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine American Bitcoin (ABTC) Posts $126 Million Profit as Holdings Gain $197 Million American Bitcoin Corp. (Nasdaq: ABTC) reported about $126 million in third-quarter net income on Wednesday, a swing from a $57.2 million loss in the prior quarter that rested largely on a $197.3 million gain on the company’s bitcoin holdings rather than on mining revenue. The Miami-based miner and treasury company, a majority-owned subsidiary of Hut 8 Corp. and co-founded with Trump family backing, mined about 891 bitcoin in the quarter at a cost of roughly $42,100 each and ended September with about 8,427 BTC. Mining revenue was about $63.4 million, down from about $67.0 million in the second quarter. Gross profit was about $25.8 million, a 41% margin, compared with about $33.0 million and 49% a quarter earlier, as seasonal power costs rose across its sites. Adjusted EBITDA came in at about $221 million, compared with an Adjusted EBITDA loss of about $45.0 million in the second quarter, according to the company’s release . Eric Trump, co-founder and chief strategy officer of American Bitcoin, said the quarter delivered the net income and Adjusted EBITDA figures while growing the bitcoin reserve and bitcoin per share. Chief Executive Mike Ho said the company kept mining at a structural discount to spot and raised satoshis per share by about 5% without issuing shares through its at-the-market program or buying bitcoin on the open market. A paper gain carried American Bitcoin’s quarter The income statement makes the driver plain. American Bitcoin booked a $197.3 million gain on digital assets in the third quarter, after a $71.2 million loss on that line in the second. Operating income was about $191.8 million. Other expense included a $64.3 million loss on derivatives. Strip the mark-to-market move out of the picture and the operating story looks quieter. Revenue per bitcoin mined was about $71,100, down slightly from about $71,900 in the second quarter, and the cost to mine rose to about $42,100 from about $36,500, the company said. Production of about 891 bitcoin was below the second quarter’s roughly 932 coins, which the company had called its highest quarterly haul on record when it reported a $57.2 million second-quarter loss alongside a climb in holdings to about 8,002 BTC. American Bitcoin said it sold a portion of production to cover operating costs while still adding to its strategic reserve. Holdings rose by about 425 bitcoin, or about 5%, to roughly 8,427 as of Sept. 30. That total includes about 3,090 bitcoin pledged for miner purchases under agreements with Bitmain. Reserve up, satoshis per share up Management’s preferred yardstick is satoshis per share, which rose about 5% to roughly 11,572 from about 10,989 at the end of June. The share count reflects a 1-for-15 reverse stock split effected earlier this year on July 2. The owned fleet stood at about 89,242 bitcoin miners with roughly 28.1 EH/s of capacity at quarter-end. item.title: Judge Lets Stock Perpetual Futures Keep Trading but Says CFTC Likely Overstepped Its Authority
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Judge Lets Stock Perpetual Futures Keep Trading but Says CFTC Likely Overstepped Its Authority Stock perpetual futures can keep trading on Kalshi, Coinbase Derivatives and Bitnomial for now after a federal judge denied an emergency bid to halt them Tuesday, while finding that the Wall Street-backed challengers are likely to prove the CFTC overstepped its authority. U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni denied the temporary restraining order on Nov. 3 after a teleconference with the parties, hours after the CFTC said the products could begin trading on U.S.-regulated exchanges. The plaintiff is the Capital Markets Alliance Association, a New York nonprofit whose members include Cboe Global Markets, Citadel Securities and the Healthy Markets Association, according to a declaration from its secretary, Adam Ford. The group sued the CFTC and Chairman Michael S. Selig in the Southern District of New York, case No. 1:26-cv-09608, seeking to undo the approvals of filings by all three exchanges. Caproni wrote that the group “is likely to succeed on the merits” of its claim that the agency lacks statutory authority to allow perpetual derivatives on individual stocks to be offered to retail investors on CFTC-regulated platforms. “Because the perpetual contracts, by definition, do not provide for a ‘sale for future delivery of a single security,’ they cannot be a security future over which the CFTC has statutory and regulatory authority,” she wrote. Instead, she said, the contracts “appear to satisfy the definition of a swap,” which falls to the Securities and Exchange Commission. She also found that the balance of equities and the public interest favor the alliance, writing that the agency’s actions “seem to represent a major disruption to the equities market.” The request failed on one prong. Caproni said the declarations from Cboe, Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets were “conjectural” about the harm members would suffer and did not show irreparable harm that was “actual and imminent.” What the ruling does and does not do The order leaves the approvals in place. It does not decide the case or the alliance’s separate motion for a preliminary injunction. The CFTC’s opposition is due Friday, Nov. 6, and the alliance’s reply is due Tuesday, Nov. 10. The order says that schedule is subject to change by the assigned judge. The docket lists Judge Lorna G. Schofield as assigned to the case. Kalshi was already listing four single-stock perps on Qualcomm, McDonald’s, Amgen and Costco by Wednesday morning, with maximum leverage of 4.9 times. Bloomberg Law reported that the judge signaled she might ultimately side with the Wall Street firms opposed to the products. A CFTC-SEC turf fight with crypto venues in the middle The fight is over a label. Selig’s Nov. 3 statement said the contracts were deemed approved under Commission Regulation 40.3 as security futures products, a category the CFTC and SEC oversee jointly. item.title: Huizenga Loses House Seat Despite $1 Million From Crypto PAC Fairshake
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Huizenga Loses House Seat Despite $1 Million From Crypto PAC Fairshake Rep. Bill Huizenga, the No. 2 Republican on the House Financial Services Committee, lost his reelection bid to Democrat Sean McCann, the Associated Press called Wednesday afternoon, despite about $1 million in support from the crypto super PAC Fairshake. With more than 97% of votes counted earlier today, McCann led Huizenga 50.1% to 48.3% in Michigan’s 4th Congressional District, a gap of about 7,000 votes out of nearly 300,000 cast. The race had been rated “lean Republican” heading into Tuesday. Huizenga, an eight-term congressman and the committee’s vice chair, is the highest-ranking Republican on the panel to lose. He is not the only crypto ally on it to go down. Rep. Bryan Steil of Wisconsin, who chairs the Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology and Artificial Intelligence, lost to Democrat Mitchell Berman 52% to 48%. The AP called that race at 11:48 p.m. Tuesday. Rep. Ann Wagner of Missouri, who chairs the capital markets subcommittee, lost to Democrat Fred Wellman. Rep. Zach Nunn of Iowa lost to state Sen. Sarah Trone Garriott, and Rep. Mike Lawler of New York conceded to Democrat Cait Conley before the AP called his race. Fairshake’s $1 million bets come up short Fairshake committed at least $1 million in October to each of six House incumbents, among them Huizenga, Steil and committee Chairman French Hill of Arkansas. The super PAC reported spending $1,019,166 to support Huizenga in the general election, according to Federal Election Commission filings. All 32 House incumbents the Fairshake network backed this fall voted for the CLARITY Act when it passed the House 294-134 in July 2025, CNBC reported. The network entered September with about $120.4 million in cash. The crypto money was a small slice of the Huizenga race. Outside groups reported more than $25 million in spending in the district, FEC filings show, with House Majority PAC alone putting about $6 million against the Republican. Two of Fairshake’s three Republican $1 million picks on the committee have now lost in midterms. Hill’s own race had not been called by the AP as of Wednesday afternoon. He led Democrat Chris Jones by about 4,400 votes, or 50.9% to 49.1%, with 99% of the expected vote counted. What the losses mean for crypto in the House Democrats won control of the House on Tuesday, which hands the committee gavel to their side regardless of Hill’s result. Rep. Maxine Waters of California, the panel’s top Democrat and its chair from 2019 to 2023, is in line to return to the post. Nineteen Financial Services Democrats backed her in October against a possible challenge from Rep. Sean Casten of Illinois, Politico reported. Steil’s loss also leaves the digital assets subcommittee without its chair. Huizenga sat on that panel too. item.title: French Bank Credit Mutuel Arkea Confirms Cyberattack as ZachXBT Puts Losses Above $133 Million
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine French Bank Credit Mutuel Arkea Confirms Cyberattack as ZachXBT Puts Losses Above $133 Million French bank Credit Mutuel Arkea said Wednesday that a cyberattack allowed hackers to carry out fraudulent transfers from the bank’s own account, a theft that on-chain investigator ZachXBT has put at more than $133 million and that the bank has not confirmed. The Brittany-based lender said in a statement that the incident was under control, that operations were resuming and that customer assets were not affected. It suspended some transactions as a precaution. “This incident has had no impact on (customer) assets and has only caused a delay in the execution of certain transfers,” the bank said on its website, in a translation published by Reuters . In a follow-up question-and-answer note , Credit Mutuel Arkea said the attackers went through the platform of one of its service providers and reached the bank directly. They used the bank’s own account to send transactions to other banks, which then potentially allowed them to convert the money into cryptocurrency through specialized platforms, the bank said. No customer accounts at its federations or subsidiaries were used, the bank said. It denied French press reports that the attackers got in through Fortuneo, its online banking arm, and said the Credit Mutuel Arkea hack was “a sophisticated attack from the outside,” not the result of human error. The size of the Credit Mutuel Arkea hack The bank has not given a final figure. Asked whether 118 million euros, or $133 million, had been stolen, it said it does not confirm the number and can only “validate the order of magnitude.” Part of the funds involved has been frozen and other steps are underway to recover the rest, the bank said. It added that the amounts at stake are “absolutely not” large enough to threaten its financial health or soundness. AFP reported that the bank put the attack at about 100 million euros in a provisional estimate. Earlier Wednesday, Reuters reported that the bank said its losses were lower than $133 million. “It is still too early to give a final figure,” a spokesperson told the wire service. What ZachXBT reported ZachXBT first flagged the incident on Monday without naming the victim. He wrote on his Telegram channel that an EU entity was suspected of losing more than $106 million from multiple centralized exchange accounts on Nov. 1, with the funds withdrawn as USDC and USDT. He said the funds were then swapped for ether and moved across several chains. In an update , he said he had found another $27 million or more in exchange withdrawals, bringing the total to more than $133 million. A later post named Credit Mutuel Arkea as the alleged victim. He wrote that the attack “occurred for multiple days” and that he suspects the amount stolen is larger once over-the-counter activity is counted. The bank has not confirmed his figure or his timeline. It has also not said when the attack began, who was behind it or whet

item.title: House Democrats Eye Their Own Crypto Market Structure Bill With a Bigger SEC Role After Sweep
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine House Democrats Eye Their Own Crypto Market Structure Bill With a Bigger SEC Role After Sweep House Democrats are discussing a plan to turn Rep. Maxine Waters’ Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights into their own crypto market structure bill next Congress, with ideas that include a bigger role for the SEC and a smaller one for the CFTC, Eleanor Terrett reported Wednesday. The proposal would fold in the Democratic Clarity Act provisions Waters offered in the House, which were not adopted, plus the provisions Senate Democrats were able to agree on with Republicans before September’s failed cloture vote. Terrett cited three industry sources who have spoken with Democratic staffers. Further ethics provisions restricting the crypto activities of President Donald Trump and other federal officials are also likely, she wrote. Republicans are calling it a “messaging bill.” No text for the crypto market structure bill has been released, and the details so far come from industry sources rather than from lawmakers. JUST IN: House Democrats reportedly want to revive their Clarity Act provisions in a broader crypto market structure bill next Congress, Eleanor Terrett reports. pic.twitter.com/8twokppjHz — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 4, 2026 The talks follow Tuesday’s Democratic sweep of Congress . Waters, the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, is in line to take the gavel in January from Chairman French Hill, the Clarity Act’s sponsor. Bloomberg Law reported Wednesday that the new majorities give Democrats leverage over the Clarity Act, the industry’s top legislative priority, starting with tougher ethics rules aimed at Trump’s ventures. What the Waters amendment would do for crypto Waters offered the bill of rights as amendment #31 to H.R. 3633 in July 2025. The House Rules Committee blocked it 4-8 along party lines, on a motion from Rep. Mary Gay Scanlon of Pennsylvania. Making an amendment “in order” lets the full House debate and vote on it, so the result kept the package off the floor. The committee’s record lists what it would have required: 24/7 customer service, insurance or SIPC-like coverage, fiduciary and best-execution rules, anti-front-running rules, bankruptcy-remote custody with 24-hour withdrawals and monthly auditor-attested proof of reserves. It would also have sent more funding to the SEC and CFTC. The committee rejected a second Democratic amendment by the same 4-8 margin. That one, from Rep. Joe Neguse of Colorado, would have barred members of Congress, presidents and vice presidents from issuing or endorsing digital assets. The ethics fight it previewed later followed the bill to the Senate. SEC versus CFTC The agency split is where a Democratic crypto market structure bill would break most sharply from the Republican one. item.title: Bitcoin Price Holds Near $80,000 as Democratic Sweep Sparks Short Squeeze
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Holds Near $80,000 as Democratic Sweep Sparks Short Squeeze Bitcoin price traded near $80,000 on Wednesday afternoon, up about 3% on the day and roughly $26,000 below its price one year ago, as markets shook off election-night jitters over the Democratic sweep of Congress , according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. Bitcoin changed hands at $80,099 at 3:12 p.m. ET, with a market cap of about $1.61 trillion and roughly $39.6 billion in trading volume over the past 24 hours. The low came in the 10 p.m. ET hour on Tuesday, as results showed Democrats taking both chambers. The high came in the 10 a.m. hour on Wednesday. That is a swing of about 7.3% from bottom to top in roughly 12 hours. The climb was a short squeeze. About $950 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, and bets against prices made up $560 million of that. Bitcoin positions accounted for $403 million of the total, 76% of it shorts. CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju wrote on X Wednesday afternoon that $215 million in bitcoin shorts were liquidated in a single hour. JUST IN: Bitcoin surges to $81,000 pic.twitter.com/k1bGzrrzCP — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 4, 2026 The view among analysts is that the sell-off had already done its work. CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the sweep was largely priced into bitcoin before the vote, leaving room for a relief rally once the uncertainty cleared. Lumida CEO Ram Ahluwalia had laid out the same path in a podcast interview the day before the election. A Democratic sweep, he said, would bring “a one and done washout, and that resets where asset prices are.” Stocks, oil and a weaker dollar Bitcoin price did not rally alone. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose about 1,500 points, or 3%, on Wednesday afternoon, while the S&P 500 climbed 1.7% and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.8%. Apple and Microsoft touched record highs. Oil moved the most. Brent crude fell more than 9% to $93.91 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate dropped nearly 9% to $87.59 by 12:36 p.m. ET, CNBC reported, after Vice President JD Vance blamed the Republican losses on the Iran war. “The reason we lost is the war,” Vance wrote on X. That matters for bitcoin price because crude above $100 has kept inflation hot and the Federal Reserve leaning toward a December hike. The U.S. dollar index fell 0.55% to 101.32 in early trading, its lowest since Oct. 1. What comes next for bitcoin price Demand from funds has not caught up with the price. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shed $115.6 million on Tuesday, their third straight session of outflows, with BlackRock’s IBIT losing $95 million. The three-day total comes to about $1.16 billion. Wednesday’s flows will be reported after the U.S. close. The policy picture got worse for the industry, not better. item.title: Matt Corallo Flags Critical Linux Kernel Flaw; Lightning Labs Ships LND Mitigation
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Matt Corallo Flags Critical Linux Kernel Flaw; Lightning Labs Ships LND Mitigation Bitcoin Core and Lightning developer Matt Corallo highlighted a severe Linux kernel vulnerability on October 30, criticizing Ubuntu’s delayed response to what he called “the most critical Linux vuln ever.” The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-98432 , affects the kernel’s IPv4 TCP handshake code with a CVSS severity score of 9.8. Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team later showed it could be turned into a remote root exploit against systems exposing a Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener. Peter Todd echoed the warning the same day, advising anyone running LND on Linux with open ports to shut their Bitcoin Lightning nodes down until the kernel was patched or otherwise mitigated. The demonstrated exploit path relies on an MPTCP listener—something Go 1.24 and later enable by default. Because LND is written in Go , recent versions were listening with MPTCP on their peer, gRPC, and REST ports whenever the kernel had the feature enabled. Lightning Labs responded the same day with emergency releases: lnd v0.21.6-beta and the backport v0.20.7-beta . Both disable MPTCP listeners by default, closing the demonstrated exploit path through LND. The project described the change as a mitigation, not a fix, and noted that only a patched kernel fully resolves the underlying issue. Other services on the same machine remain exposed until MPTCP is disabled host-wide or the kernel is updated. Olaoluwa Osuntokun and the official Lightning Labs account both recommended the update. Security researcher Marcus Hutchins later reported internet-wide scanning activity consistent with threat actors looking for exposed systems. His scans found roughly 2.1 million servers reachable over MPTCP on port 443. International Cyber Digest amplified the finding on November 4, noting the scanning and Ubuntu’s slower patch timeline. Canonical has since made fixed kernels available in the opt-in, proposed pocket for Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04, but they have not yet reached the regular updates channel. Red Hat shipped fixes for RHEL 8/9/10 on November 1; Debian, Amazon Linux, and others had already released patches earlier. UmbrelOS 2.0.1 included the kernel fix on November 1st for x86 devices and applied a traffic-blocking mitigation on Raspberry Pi, where a fixed kernel was not yet available. No confirmed in-the-wild exploitation has been reported, and the vulnerability has not been added to CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Anthropic’s remote-root demonstration remains unpublished. The practical exposure is highest on internet-facing servers. Home desktop systems behind typical NAT and firewalls, without public TCP listeners, are far less affected. For Lightning operators on Linux, the LND releases remove the specific MPTCP listener path the public exploit used, but the broader kernel bug remains until a patched kernel is installed. item.title: Strategy’s STRC Hits $100 Par for First Time Since May After Over $2 Billion in Buybacks
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategy’s STRC Hits $100 Par for First Time Since May After Over $2 Billion in Buybacks Strategy’s Stretch preferred stock touched $100 today for the first time since May, returning to the par value the company has spent over $2 billion in buybacks and five months of rate increases to defend. STRC traded below $80 at times in June, a massive discount to its stated value. The climb back to $100 restores the price at which Strategy says it will resume issuing new shares, the mechanism that funds its bitcoin purchases. Chairman Michael Saylor had pledged to keep the stock at or above par and to hold the dividend at 12% until it got there. Two changes landed in the past week. Shareholders approved daily dividends on STRC and three other preferreds on Oct. 28 by a 99.3% vote, removing the semi-monthly ex-dividend drops that had added volatility to the price. The first daily payment went out Monday. And Strategy’s Oct. 29 filing set the November rate at 12% annualized, or $1 per share for the month. Shares of Strategy (MSTR) were up over 7% today after bitcoin jumped above $80,000. BREAKING: Michael Saylor's STRC has returned to par for the first time since May! They will start buying more bitcoin as soon as it goes above $100 pic.twitter.com/niNmngTP1j — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 4, 2026 What Stretch (STRC) is and why it slipped Stretch, the Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Stretch Preferred, launched in July 2025 at $90 with a 9% starting rate. Saylor called it the company’s “iPhone moment.” The design is a feedback loop: Strategy adjusts the dividend each month to hold the price near $100, sells new shares when it trades above par and uses the cash to buy bitcoin. It became the largest tradable preferred in the world, with a market value above $8 billion and a holder base that CEO Phong Le has put at about 80% retail. The loop broke earlier this year. STRC drifted below par in late January; Strategy raised the rate to 11.25% in February, 11.5% in March and 12% by summer, and the price kept sliding as bitcoin fell toward $65,000. At $89 the at-the-market program sat idle, cutting off the company’s cheapest funding. In late May, Strategy sold 32 BTC for about $2.5 million to cover a Stretch distribution, its first bitcoin sale since 2022, and critics raised the prospect of a “death spiral” that analysts at Benchmark and TD Cowen disputed. The fix was to buy the stock back. Strategy paused bitcoin purchases in the week of Oct. 19 and spent $204.9 million on STRC alone, part of the roughly $2.25 billion it has retired since the discount opened. Each share bought below $100 shrank the float and reduced the dividend bill at the same time. A thin cushion under the treasury The recovery matters because of what sits beneath it. item.title: Jack Dorsey’s Block (XYZ) Sets Aside $764 Million for DOJ Settlement as Bitcoin Profit Halves
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Jack Dorsey’s Block (XYZ) Sets Aside $764 Million for DOJ Settlement as Bitcoin Profit Halves Block has agreed in principle to pay $764 million to resolve a Justice Department investigation into its anti-money-laundering controls, a sum larger than the $566 million profit the company reported for the third quarter. The agreement, reached in October and disclosed in a 10-Q filed Nov. 3 , would defer for three years a criminal charge that Block failed to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering program under the Bank Secrecy Act. The gross figure is about $964 million, reduced to $764 million after credits for earlier regulatory settlements. Block has accrued the full amount and said losses above it are “reasonably possible.” The company disputes the basis and methodology of the government’s assessment, and the deal requires final approval. The settlement overshadowed a quarter in which gross profit rose 22% to $3.24 billion, with Cash App up 27% to $2.07 billion and Square up 14% to $1.16 billion, according to the company release. Bitcoin was the exception. Gross profit from the bitcoin business fell 50% to $52 million from $104 million a year earlier, and bitcoin revenue dropped 11% to $1.8 billion. A case for Block that began with a short seller The investigation dates to March 2023, when Hindenburg Research alleged that Cash App inflated user counts with duplicate and fraudulent accounts and that weak identity checks let criminals use the platform for scams and money laundering. Block called the report inaccurate and misleading. The Justice Department and SEC opened inquiries into the compliance practices and related disclosures; the SEC closed its side in March without recommending enforcement. State regulators moved first. In April 2025 the New York Department of Financial Services fined Block $40 million after finding a backlog of suspicious-activity alerts that grew from about 18,000 in 2018 to more than 169,000 by 2020, and a screening system that did not block bitcoin transfers to wallets linked to terrorism financing until exposure passed 10%. A multistate settlement in January 2025 added $80 million. Those payments account for part of the $200 million credit against the DOJ figure. The deferred prosecution structure means Block avoids a conviction if it meets the agreement’s terms over three years, a path Binance took in 2023 at a cost of $4.3 billion. The charge lands as Block pursues an industrial bank charter for a unit it calls Builders Bank, which would offer custody and fiduciary services for bitcoin. Bank regulators weigh compliance history in charter decisions. The drop in bitcoin profit was a choice. Block said the decline came from its decision to cut fees on certain Cash App bitcoin transactions, part of a push to make the asset a payment rail rather than a trading product. item.title: Librería de Satoshi Rebrands to ISMOS, Launches Global Platform to Train One Million Bitcoin Developers
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Librería de Satoshi Rebrands to ISMOS, Launches Global Platform to Train One Million Bitcoin Developers Librería de Satoshi, the technical education organization, recently announced the launch of its global platform as they rebrand to ISMOS and shows off a new website. The organization aims to expand its Bitcoin and open-source developer education program throughout the world, creating local hubs across the world and delivering education programs in local languages. Since 2021, ISMOS has reached more than 3,665 people in more than 40 countries and has financially supported 30 open-source developers, according to a press release shared with Bitcoin Magazine. “Talent is universal; opportunity is not. I founded Librería de Satoshi because I experienced the language barrier in Bitcoin firsthand. ISMOS takes that mission worldwide, so that the next great developer can come from anywhere,” said Dulce Villarreal, CEO and founder of ISMOS. What began as a Bitcoin school for Spanish speakers is today a technical education ecosystem and a complete training path for freedom technologies and open-source developers. ISMOS brings together educators and technology creators: a space to learn and teach with “Freedom Tech values, in more languages, more regions, and more disciplines, with a growing presence in universities, bootcamps, and programming communities.” ISMOS was born in Latin America as Librería de Satoshi and is now a global movement. One Million Bitcoin Developers Around the World ISMOS combines rigorous study programs, direct mentorship, and fellowships in Spanish, Portuguese, and English, and soon in more languages. Subjects will include Bitcoin, cryptography, cybersecurity, mathematics, AI, Nostr, open-source software, and open AI models. The platform is open source, and software developers can explore its open tools at github.com/ismos-xyz . Today ISMOS is primarily supported by Btrust and the Human Rights Foundation. Other organizations, such as OpenSats and the Gemini Opportunity Fund, have supported its work in the past with smaller grants, according to the press release. The announcement reflects nearly five years of growth and a deeper commitment to equal opportunity. “Someone coding in Argentina, Nigeria, or El Salvador deserves the same chance to build a first-class technical career as anyone in Silicon Valley or London.” ISMOS aims to go beyond study programs to provide individual support to the best developers through programs such as B4OS (Bitcoin 4 Open Source), fellowships, and its developer residencies: “in their language, at their level, and with the specific support they need to go further than they imagined.” Press contact Karina Conde, Director of Operations. comms@ismos.xyz This post Librería de Satoshi Rebrands to ISMOS, Launches Global Platform to Train One Million Bitcoin Developers first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Juan Galt .
